title.en: Figurative language in sports and weather
title.es: Lenguaje figurado en deporte y clima

es: Interpretar el lenguaje figurado de una crónica deportiva, de un parte meteorológico y de una columna de opinión: localizar la expresión, explicar qué quiere decir en realidad y valorar la actitud del hablante.

teaching.en: City crushed United 3–0 on Saturday, and the radio commentary said that their defence was a wall that no striker could climb.
teaching.es: El City aplastó al United por 3–0 el sábado, y el comentario de la radio dijo que su defensa era un muro que ningún delantero podía escalar.
teaching.explanationEs: Crushed = ganó con mucha claridad; a wall = una defensa que nadie puede pasar. Commentary es el comentario en directo.
segments: City crushed United 3–0 on Saturday, and the radio commentary said
that their defence was a wall that no striker could climb.
teaching.audioText: City crushed United 3–0 on Saturday, and the radio commentary said that their defence was a wall that no striker could climb.

teaching.en: After the first goal the visitors looked like a sinking ship, and nothing their captain shouted seemed able to turn the tide.
teaching.es: Tras el primer gol los visitantes parecían un barco que se hunde, y nada de lo que gritó su capitán parecía capaz de cambiar el rumbo del partido.
teaching.explanationEs: A sinking ship = un equipo que se desmorona; turn the tide = invertir una situación adversa.
segments: After the first goal the visitors looked like a sinking ship,
and nothing their captain shouted seemed able to turn the tide.
teaching.audioText: After the first goal the visitors looked like a sinking ship, and nothing their captain shouted seemed able to turn the tide.

teaching.en: The second half was a rollercoaster, with three goals in ten minutes and a crowd that could hardly stay in their seats.
teaching.es: La segunda parte fue una montaña rusa, con tres goles en diez minutos y un público que apenas podía quedarse sentado.
teaching.explanationEs: A rollercoaster = muchas subidas y bajadas de emoción en poco tiempo.
segments: The second half was a rollercoaster, with three goals in ten
minutes and a crowd that could hardly stay in their seats.
teaching.audioText: The second half was a rollercoaster, with three goals in ten minutes and a crowd that could hardly stay in their seats.

teaching.en: The forecast says that a blanket of snow will cover the hills by midnight, so the outlook for the weekend is bleak.
teaching.es: El pronóstico dice que un manto de nieve cubrirá las colinas a medianoche, así que las perspectivas para el fin de semana son sombrías.
teaching.explanationEs: A blanket of snow = una capa que lo cubre todo; bleak describe un panorama poco esperanzador.
segments: The forecast says that a blanket of snow will cover the
hills by midnight, so the outlook for the weekend is bleak.
teaching.audioText: The forecast says that a blanket of snow will cover the hills by midnight, so the outlook for the weekend is bleak.

teaching.en: Storm clouds are gathering over the coast, which means that anyone planning a picnic should take an umbrella and avoid the beach.
teaching.es: Se están acumulando nubes de tormenta sobre la costa, lo que significa que quien planee un pícnic debería llevar paraguas y evitar la playa.
teaching.explanationEs: Are gathering personifica las nubes: se reúnen como personas; el sentido real es que va a llover.
segments: Storm clouds are gathering over the coast, which means that anyone
planning a picnic should take an umbrella and avoid the beach.
teaching.audioText: Storm clouds are gathering over the coast, which means that anyone planning a picnic should take an umbrella and avoid the beach.

teaching.en: By Friday the sun should chase the clouds away, although the forecast admits that this promise is not completely certain.
teaching.es: Hacia el viernes el sol debería ahuyentar las nubes, aunque el pronóstico admite que esa promesa no es del todo segura.
teaching.explanationEs: Chase away: el sol actúa como un perseguidor; el sentido real es que saldrá el sol.
segments: By Friday the sun should chase the clouds away, although
the forecast admits that this promise is not completely certain.
teaching.audioText: By Friday the sun should chase the clouds away, although the forecast admits that this promise is not completely certain.

prompt.es: Según la crónica, ¿qué significan «crushed» y «a wall»?

choices.text: A narrow win, with a goalkeeper who saved all the attacks.
A heavy loss, with defenders who left the door open.
A very clear win, with defenders who allowed no chances.

feedback.es: El marcador 4–0 y el dato de que los visitantes no tuvieron ninguna ocasión confirman una victoria clara y una defensa impenetrable.

hint.es: Fíjate en el marcador y en que los visitantes nunca tuvieron una ocasión de marcar.

origin.text: The home team crushed the visitors 4–0. Their defence was a wall, and the visitors never had a single chance to score during the whole afternoon.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se están acumulando nubes de tormenta sobre la costa.»

feedback.es: Are gathering personifica las nubes: se reúnen antes de la lluvia y por eso los barcos deben volver al puerto.

hint.es: Es un verbo en -ing que significa «reunirse» y se aplica a las nubes como si fueran personas.

origin.text: The forecast warns that storm clouds are ___ over the coast. By evening the wind will rise, so anyone sailing should return to harbour before dark.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El sol debería ahuyentar las nubes hacia el mediodía.»

answer.text: The sun should chase the clouds away by noon

feedback.es: Chase away personifica el sol como alguien que echa las nubes; by noon indica el momento.

hint.es: Empieza con The sun should y termina con by noon.

prompt.es: Escucha el parte y elige cuándo se despejará la niebla.

choices.text: Early in the morning, before nine o'clock.
Around noon, when the storm arrives.
Late in the evening, after the traffic.

feedback.es: El sol ahuyentará la niebla antes de las nueve; la tormenta llega hacia el mediodía y el tráfico es del viaje de esta noche.

origin.audio: Good evening, and here is tomorrow's forecast. A thick blanket of fog will cover the valley at dawn, and storm clouds will be gathering over the hills by noon. Fortunately, the sun will chase the fog away before nine, so the morning should be bright. Anyone driving to the coast tonight should leave early, because the roads will be busy.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión figurada con su sentido real.

pairs.es: una capa de nieve que lo cubre todo

feedback.es: Cada imagen describe algo real: un equipo en crisis, una nevada que cubre el suelo, un partido cambiante y una defensa sólida.

pairs.es: una capa de nieve que lo cubre todo

prompt.es: ¿Qué quiere decir la crónica con «rollercoaster» en este párrafo?

choices.text: The match was slow and kept the fans waiting.
The match changed quickly and kept the fans tense.
The match was violent and the referee lost control.

feedback.es: Dos goles, un penalti y una tarjeta roja en pocos minutos y un público que no aparta la vista describen un partido de altibajos.

origin.text: Match report: The visitors started the second half like a rollercoaster: two goals, then a penalty, then a red card, all before the hour. Nobody in the stadium dared to look away from the pitch.

prompt.es: Escucha el comentario y elige qué actitud adopta el comentarista ante la queja.

choices.text: He takes the complaint seriously and blames the referee for the result.
He has no opinion and only reports what the manager said.
He thinks the complaint is weak, because City was clearly better.

feedback.es: Describe un City muy superior y termina con los aficionados riéndose: deja entender que la queja del entrenador no tiene fundamento.

origin.audio: What a night for City! Their defence was a wall, and the visitors never found a way through. After ten minutes United were already a sinking ship, and the second goal crushed whatever hope they had left. Yet their manager insisted that the result was unfair, and he complained that the referee had handed City the game. The fans at the back of the stadium just laughed.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué implica «a sinking ship» sobre el United.

choices.text: They lost control early and could not turn the tide.
They were playing well until the referee changed the game.
They started badly but recovered well before the break.

feedback.es: A sinking ship tras solo diez minutos y un segundo gol que aplasta su esperanza indican un equipo que se hunde sin reaccionar.

origin.audio: What a night for City! Their defence was a wall, and the visitors never found a way through. After ten minutes United were already a sinking ship, and the second goal crushed whatever hope they had left. Yet their manager insisted that the result was unfair, and he complained that the referee had handed City the game. The fans at the back of the stadium just laughed.

prompt.es: Completa: «Durante la noche un manto de nieve cubrió el pueblo.»

feedback.es: A blanket of snow presenta la nieve como una manta que cubre y abriga al pueblo; sleeping under it, warm and soft refuerza esa imagen (mantle y layer también se aceptan).

origin.text: During the night a ___ of snow covered the village, and when the children woke up, every street was still sleeping under it, warm and soft.

prompt.es: ¿Qué opina el columnista de decir «aplastó» tras cada 3–0?

choices.text: It is accurate because City was far stronger from the start.
It is a habit that forgets how City really won.
It is exaggerated only when the defence is very weak.

feedback.es: El columnista considera el adjetivo una costumbre perezosa: el partido se ganó con paciencia, no con una superioridad aplastante.

origin.text: Some commentators say that City crushed United after every 3–0 win. I think the phrase is lazy. Saturday's game was not like that; it was patient: City kept the ball, waited, and let United make mistakes. The wall in defence mattered less than patience in attack.

prompt.es: ¿Qué consejo implícito da este parte del tiempo?

choices.text: Leave the umbrella at home, because the sun will return.
Stay indoors all day, because the storm starts at noon.
Carry an umbrella, because the dry weather will not last.

feedback.es: El parte anuncia tormenta por la tarde y una única hora de sol incierta: lo prudente es llevar paraguas.

origin.text: Forecast: a blanket of cloud will sit over the city all day, and storm clouds will be gathering from the west by evening. The sun may chase the cloud away for an hour at noon, but nobody should count on it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los aficionados llamaron montaña rusa a la segunda parte.»

feedback.es: Rollercoaster es la metáfora de un partido con muchos altibajos: aquí el liderato cambia tres veces en diez minutos.

origin.text: The fans called the second half a ___ because the lead changed hands three times in ten minutes, and nobody in the stadium could relax for a second.

prompt.es: Escucha la noticia y elige qué deja entender la hablante sobre la prensa.

choices.text: That the press changed its view once the team won.
That the press still doubted the team after the win.
That the press blamed the league leaders for losing.

feedback.es: Los mismos periódicos que decían que no tenían esperanza hablan ahora de un punto de inflexión: cambian de opinión al ver el resultado.

origin.audio: The local team were a sinking ship for most of the season. Yesterday, however, they crushed the league leaders in the final minutes, and suddenly everything changed. Today the same newspapers that said they had no hope are describing the result as a turning point.
